issues.legal_issue: The appropriate method for valuing an orchard is to capitalize its net income using a multiplier suited to the nature and expected yielding life of its trees and the other circumstances.
material_facts: Compensation was assessed for land containing coconut and orange topes acquired for a public project.
The valuation officer capitalized the topes’ net income using a 20-year purchase multiplier, after finding that the fruit-bearing trees would yield for more than 20 years.
The reference court increased the estimated yield and produce prices but retained the multiplier; the High Court considered the method fair.
The State challenged the multiplier, relying on an earlier decision that had used a 10-year purchase multiplier for a coconut garden.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that capitalizing the net income at 20 years’ purchase was a fair and reasonable method in the circumstances, and dismissed the appeals.
issues.legal_principle: The approved method for valuing orchards is to capitalize net income at a number of years’ purchase fixed with reference to the nature of the trees and other circumstances. The Court relied on Kompalli Nageshwara Rao v. Special Deputy Collector, Land Acquisition, which applied that approach, and Elias M. Cohen v. Secretary of State, which capitalized orchard income at 15 years’ purchase. It distinguished Shunmuga Velayuda Mudaliar v. Collector of Tanjore because that decision gave no reasoned principle for selecting 10 years’ purchase. The Court also noted that Rajammal v. Head Quarters Deputy Collector, Vellore had used 20 years’ annual rental for long-lived, productive mango trees.

predicates.land_acquisition_valuation_appeal: The matter was an appeal concerning compensation for land acquired by the state.
predicates.orchard_valued_by_net_income_capitalizat: The valuation officer assessed an orchard by capitalizing its net income.
predicates.trees_expected_to_yield_for_period_suppo: The valuation officer found that the trees were expected to yield for a period supporting the multiplier selected.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns acquired land and the orchard’s net income was capitalized using a multiplier supported by the trees’ expected yielding life, the capitalization method is fair.
